channel.description: Personally scored technology & science articles curated by news-filter

item.title: Google offers free Gemini Tasks for AI-powered automation
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Gemini can now do more than chat, and Google is making it free
Google is offering free access to Gemini Tasks in six countries, expanding its AI assistant beyond chat to handle automation. The feature, previously available only to paid subscribers, can manage multi-step projects, build travel itineraries, schedule briefings, automate research, and handle household chores. It runs in the background, sends completion notifications, and allows users to add instructions. Available in the US, India, Canada, Australia, Japan, and South Korea, Gemini Tasks is now part of the main Gemini app. The AI can also make phone calls to compare prices, check inventory, and schedule appointments, identifying itself as an AI assistant. Google Pay integration tracks product availability and price drops, preparing purchases within user-defined limits, though users must approve transactions. Gemini can also process text messages and emails, extracting info and organizing tasks. The update reflects a shift toward AI agents that act independently, though challenges like website restrictions and errors remain. Google emphasizes user control with approval requirements for sensitive actions.

item.title: Nvidia Rebuffs Claims It Predicted Agentic Moment in Vera Development
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Nvidia says it’s ‘absurd’ to assume it predicted the agentic moment during Vera’s development
Ian Finder, Nvidia’s head of data center CPU business, dismissed claims that the company predicted the agentic moment during Vera’s development as 'absurd.' He emphasized Nvidia’s design intuition and co-design approach with accelerators rather than explicitly targeting agentic workloads. Vera’s 'opinionated' features, including an opinionated memory system via Nvidia’s Scalable Coherency Fabric and Olympus microarchitecture, reflect a clean-sheet design aimed at future AI agent demands. Finder contrasted Nvidia’s approach with legacy constraints from Intel and AMD, noting the CPU’s focus on memory bandwidth and concurrency rather than dollar-per-core economics. While Vera doesn’t excel at all workloads, its memory advantages position it for agentic computing. Finder clarified that while Vera wasn’t designed around today’s agents, early signs of tool calling and head node requirements hinted at the trend. He argued that agentic workloads require both GPUs and CPUs, with GPUs handling model inference and CPUs managing compilation and testing. Nvidia’s Vera, alongside startups like Daytona and E2B, aims to optimize memory systems for rapid sandbox creation, with future CPUs like Rosa set to follow.

item.title: Windows Server 2028 Introduces Hardened Security by Default
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Windows Server 2028 trades compatibility for out-of-the-box security
Microsoft introduced Windows Server 2028 Public Preview with a security-by-default approach called Hardened Server Core. The new framework aligns with Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) benchmarks. Previously, administrators had to manually configure security settings, but now secure configurations are the default starting state. This change applies only to Server Core installations, excluding Desktop Experience versions. Key security updates include Kerberos as the default over NTLM, TLS restricted to modern cipher suites, hybrid post-quantum key exchange using quantum-safe ML-KEM, and stricter remote desktop and PowerShell script block logging. Administrators still retain control over active security protocols but benefit from reduced initial exposure. Microsoft emphasizes that the hardened baseline closes the window where newly deployed servers remain unsecured during setup.

item.title: Nvidia Reports $115.8 Billion Revenue, Vera Rubin Drives $20 Billion in Q3 2027
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Nvidia's revenue hits $115.8 billion as Vera Rubin generates $20 billion in another record-setting quarter
Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in revenue for Q3 fiscal 2027, with its Vera Rubin platform generating $20 billion. The company's supply commitments surged to $390 billion, driven by multiyear memory agreements. Colette Kress, interim CEO, highlighted Vera Rubin's rapid product ramp as the fastest in Nvidia's history, with hyperscale partners bringing systems into production in one month. Data Center revenue reached $107.6 billion, up 21% sequentially, while AI Clouds, Industrial & Enterprise sales hit $47.5 billion, up 195% YoY. Nvidia expects FY2028 revenue growth to rise to 75% due to expanded manufacturing capacity. The company disclosed $32 billion in neocloud agreements and $118 billion in credit guarantees, including $105 billion for OpenAI's Ohio data center. GAAP gross margin is projected to decline to 71%-72% in Q4, with revised pricing planned for FY2028 to offset supply costs. Kress avoided direct comments on custom AI accelerators' impact on Nvidia's pricing power.

item.title: Microsoft Introduces Tool to Centralize PC Security Checks
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Original headline: Microsoft’s new tool checks your PC’s core security in one place
Microsoft is rolling out Windows Baseline Protection, a tool that consolidates core security features into a single dashboard. The tool checks Secure Boot, TPM security processor, memory integrity, virtualization-based security, and protection against unsafe drivers. Users can enable most protections with a single click and a restart, or receive step-by-step guidance for UEFI settings. The feature is accessible via Windows Settings under Security. Microsoft is offering the tool in preview to Windows Insider Program participants and plans general availability in 2027. The tool simplifies meeting Microsoft’s basic security requirements by centralizing existing protections.

item.title: Google Enforces Foldable App Standards Starting 2027
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central, Digital Trends Original headline: Google Enforces Foldable-Ready Standards for Android Apps Starting in 2027
Google is enforcing new adaptive quality rules for Android apps starting April 2027. All apps must meet Tier 3 standards for foldable compatibility to remain on Google Play, with non-compliant apps facing reduced visibility. The changes address letterboxing on large displays, a common issue with foldable devices. Over 580 million large-screen devices are in use, prompting the update. Tier 3 requires apps to fill available screens without letterboxing, maintain scroll positions during folds, and support multi-window environments. Developers must submit three foldable screenshots by April 2027, with games required to comply by that date. Higher tiers, Tier 2 and Tier 1, add features like external accessory support and camera continuity, offering premium badges and better merchandising. Developers must target Android 17’s API level 37 by August 2027, ending opt-outs for orientation locks. Mishaal Rahman noted games will have a slightly extended timeline for Tier 3 compliance. The framework builds on prior efforts to improve app adaptability across devices, prioritizing hardware capabilities.
item.source: Latest from Android Central, Digital Trends

item.title: Google adds incognito mode for AI Mode in Search
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Google’s AI feature in Search gets its own incognito mode
Google is adding an incognito-like mode to its AI Mode in Search, allowing temporary conversations that don’t appear in search history or recommendations. The feature, called 'temporary threads,' lets users start a chat via an icon in AI Mode’s interface. Once activated, the session detaches from the user’s account, meaning past preferences don’t influence future responses, and the chat isn’t saved. This aims to prevent personal conversations from affecting search personalization. The option is rolling out globally on desktop and mobile across all supported languages. Google notes that temporary chats function similarly to standalone Gemini chatbots, offering privacy for sensitive or one-off queries. Users can close the thread to return to normal search without lingering data.

item.title: Global OLED Monitor Shipments Double in Q3 2026
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Global OLED monitor shipments doubled year-over-year in Q3 2026
Global OLED monitor shipments doubled year-over-year in Q3 2026, according to TrendForce. Shipments rose 13% sequentially, driven by falling prices, improved technology, and aggressive marketing. ASUS led with 21.7% market share, followed by MSI at 14.5% and Samsung at 11.3%. Omdia reports mainstream 27-inch QHD 240Hz OLED gaming monitors saw price cuts exceeding 40% in 2026. Newer tandem OLED panels offer better brightness and color reproduction, while RGB-stripe layouts improve text rendering. OLEDs are becoming viable for everyday use, not just gaming. AI industry demand for memory and storage has inflated PC upgrade costs, but monitors face less supply pressure. OLEDs provide superior contrast, response times, and HDR performance compared to LCDs. Despite concerns about burn-in and lifespan, OLED remains the best display technology available. Several top gaming monitors use OLED, making it a compelling upgrade for gamers.

item.title: Starlink Gains 4 US Subscribers for Every One Lost
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Starlink Is Gaining 4 US Subscribers for Every One It Loses, Research Finds
Starlink is gaining four US subscribers for every one lost to competition, according to ST3 Insights. Eric Fogle, founder of ST3 Insights, says the company tracks actual users via anonymized app installs and IP address analysis. In Q3, 120,114 users switched from other ISPs to Starlink, with 27,000 from Spectrum, 17,000 from Xfinity, and 41,000 from fixed wireless providers. Conversely, 29,240 Starlink users moved to ground-based services, mostly Spectrum and Xfinity. The net gain was 90,874 subscribers, despite a May price increase. Growth was strongest in Texas, California, Arizona, and Virginia. Fogle notes SpaceX may face tougher competition as it expands into areas with multiple ISPs. Starlink recently introduced 30-50% discounts in some regions, lowering rates to as low as $27.50 monthly, though pricing could change.

item.title: Microsoft’s AI coders challenge Claude and ChatGPT with cost advantages
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Microsoft’s new AI coder is gunning for Claude and ChatGPT. It’s coming with a price advantage
Microsoft introduced two new AI coding models, MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash, at Ignite 2026. The models compete with OpenAI’s GPT-6 Sol and Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5, offering similar performance at significantly lower costs. MAI Code 2 claims 98% of GPT-6 Sol’s performance at 40% of its cost and 96% of Claude Opus 5.5’s performance at 5% of its price. Developers preferred MAI Code 2’s frontend designs over GPT-6 Sol in 64% of blind comparisons. MAI Code 2 Flash focuses on speed, matching GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5’s performance at 65% and 20% of their costs, respectively. Both models are available via GitHub Copilot, with MAI Code 2 accessible to Pro and Enterprise subscribers, and Flash available to Free and Student users. Microsoft also expanded its AI portfolio to include cybersecurity, image generation, and real-time voice models. The company noted the models are optimized for coding tasks but not yet suited for complex scientific research or long-running agentic tasks, using promotional pricing for comparisons.

item.title: MacPaw's iPhone Security App Detects Scam Texts
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: MacPaw brings its security app to iPhone, and it can spot scam texts before you fall for them
MacPaw has released Moonlock for iPhone, expanding its security app to mobile devices. The app includes Scam Detect, which analyzes suspicious texts, screenshots, or QR codes to identify potential scams. Safe SMS automatically flags and isolates suspected scam messages from unknown senders. Additional features include a Security Score, Email Breach History, and device checks for Wi-Fi safety and iOS updates. Moonlock is free to download but offers subscription tiers starting at $9.99 monthly or $49.99 annually. It requires iOS 26.0 or later and does not scan for malware due to Apple's restrictions on third-party app access. Privacy measures include local processing of data and limited access to new messages only. The app lacks features like malware scanning present in the Mac version but provides targeted security tools for iPhone users.

item.title: Proton Launches Privacy-Focused AI Assistant for PCs
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Original headline: Proton launches a privacy-first AI assistant for your PC
Proton has released Lumo Desktop, a privacy-focused AI assistant for PCs. The app allows users to search documents, access Google Drive and Proton Mail, and interact with local folders. It includes features like Schedules for automating recurring tasks and Skills for reusable task instructions. Users control which actions Lumo can perform automatically, requiring approval or blocking certain functions. The AI does not use conversation or connected app data for training models, and chat history is encrypted to prevent even Proton from accessing content. Lumo Desktop is available for Windows, Linux, and macOS, requiring a Proton account. The app emphasizes privacy by limiting data access and ensuring encryption protections.

item.title: Microsoft Enhances Copilot with File Management and Troubleshooting Tools
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends, PCMag Original headline: Microsoft Expands Copilot's Capabilities with Enhanced File Management and Troubleshooting Tools
Microsoft is expanding Copilot's capabilities with new file management and troubleshooting tools. Announced at Microsoft Ignite 2026, the Hybrid Intelligence Initiative combines on-device AI models using a device's NPU with cloud processing. Copilot will manage local files via natural language commands, reducing manual editing. Users can issue verbal instructions instead of navigating file systems, with containment and identity features limiting AI operations to defined boundaries. Privacy is prioritized through read-only mode and explicit user permission for file access. Copilot provides step-by-step guidance after permission is granted. Microsoft has reduced Copilot integrations in low-adoption Windows utilities like Snipping Tool and Notepad. During a demo, Copilot resolved Bluetooth headphone issues by analyzing system data and suggesting solutions, though it could not fully diagnose problems without additional access. It identified misconfigurations like incorrect sound output endpoints but has limited diagnostic scope. The feature is in early development, with Microsoft emphasizing practical AI applications over superficial integrations. Future updates may allow Copilot to autonomously adjust settings to resolve issues.

item.title: Banks Hold Customers Liable for AI Tool Mishaps, Hacking
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: More banks say customers using AI agents are on their own — even if they get hacked
Citibank, JPMorgan, Bank of America, and PNC updated terms to hold customers fully responsible for AI tool mishaps, including hacking. Citi’s policy states customers bear liability for transactions made by third-party AI agents, even if the tool leaks credentials or is breached. A spokesperson said customers must understand risks of sharing banking credentials with AI tools. Similar policies from major banks reflect growing concerns over AI’s role in financial services. Anthropic’s new read-only personal finance tool highlights industry caution, as banks view AI as a competitive threat. Financial institutions warn customers that AI agents cannot be trusted to manage accounts securely, shifting liability to users. The shift follows AI startups’ push into personal finance, raising questions about consumer trust and bank margins. Banks argue AI tools could undermine their revenue streams by helping customers avoid fees or low-interest accounts.

item.title: Google Adds YouTube Premium Family to AI Ultra Subscriptions
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central, Digital Trends Original headline: Google Expands AI Ultra Benefits to Include Free YouTube Premium Family Access
Google has added YouTube Premium Family access to its AI Ultra subscription plans at no extra cost. Both Ultra 5x ($99.99/month) and Ultra 20x ($199.99/month) tiers now include the Family plan, allowing subscribers to share ad-free YouTube and YouTube Music with up to five family members in eligible countries. Existing AI Ultra subscribers will automatically receive the upgrade if they are family group managers. Shimrit Ben-Yair, Google’s lead for AI subscriptions, confirmed the update, calling it a requested feature. The Family plan includes background playback, offline downloads, and video queuing. While AI Ultra subscribers gain YouTube Premium Family, the AI Pro tier still lacks YouTube Music. Google aims to enhance AI subscription value by bundling popular services. Users can create family groups but may only switch plans once every 12 months. Restrictions and country eligibility apply, though the change aligns with Google’s strategy to integrate YouTube Premium discounts with AI plans.
item.source: Latest from Android Central, Digital Trends

item.title: Smartphone Thermal Tool Predicts Diabetic Foot Ulcer Healing
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: A smartphone camera could help doctors identify diabetic foot ulcers that won’t heal
A smartphone-based thermal imaging tool called TherMUL may help identify diabetic foot ulcers that won’t heal. Over 500 million people with diabetes face risks of foot ulcers, which often require four-week follow-ups to assess healing. Delays in care can lead to infections or amputations. RMIT University researchers developed TherMUL, pairing a smartphone with a FLIR One thermal camera to capture heat patterns from a foot wound without contact. The software analyzes texture features like uneven warmth to predict healing potential. In trials at two Melbourne hospitals, the model correctly identified 76% of non-healing ulcers but only 53% of healing cases. While results are modest, the tool could enable earlier intervention for patients in remote areas lacking access to specialists. Researchers note limitations, including environmental factors affecting thermal readings and the need for larger trials. TherMUL is designed to support, not replace, clinical judgment.

item.title: European workers stay in jobs but feel stuck due to limited prospects
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Report finds workers are staying around at their jobs — but many say that's because they feel stuck
Workday's European Workforce Report shows rising job retention rates, with Germany at 78.8% and all European markets exceeding the global 69.6% average. However, 34% of workers in the UK, France, and Germany say they feel stuck in their roles due to limited career prospects. Over half (54%) feel their employers don't care about them personally, and only 62% believe their companies help build needed skills. Despite AI training, fewer than 40% in key markets expect it to create career opportunities. Angelique De Vries-Schipperijn, Workday's EMEA president, warns that high retention rates mask underlying issues, noting AI is disrupting jobs and workers need clearer paths forward. Many job seekers use AI tools to find new roles, but only 34% say it led to more applications.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Hackers Exploited Multiple Platforms to Attack 178 Websites
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Hack of 178 Websites Began Quietly Days Earlier on Other Platforms
Hackers exploited multiple platforms to attack 178 websites by distributing malicious JavaScript. The campaign began days earlier, with the hacker compromising AI platform Optimizely on Monday and other services like Kissmetrics and StorifyMe on Friday. Alon Gal of Hudson Rock noted the attack spanned multiple vendors, using third-party integrations to target visitors. Malicious code aimed to steal cryptocurrency, credit card details, and cookies. Security Bank’s Philippines site was infected via Kissmetrics on Friday, while a German newspaper site used StorifyMe. Foxsports.com was hit via Minute-ly on Monday. Optimizely confirmed a vulnerability was exploited but blocked the code within three hours. StorifyMe reported a subset of customers were affected, while Kissmetrics and Minute-ly did not respond. All malicious domains were taken down. Optimizely stated less than 5% of customers were impacted.

item.title: Payhawk raises $280M in Series C, hits $2B valuation
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Spend management platform Payhawk announces $280M raise, 2B valuation
U.K.-based fintech Payhawk raised $280 million in Series C funding, led by Goldman Sachs’ growth equity arm, valuing the company at $2 billion. The round brings Payhawk’s total funding to over $500 million. Founded in 2018, the company provides enterprise financial management tools using AI agents to track expenses and procurement. CEO Hristo Borisov told FinTech magazine the funding enables growth and development of AI-native products combining agents, payment infrastructure, and enterprise controls. Payhawk competes with Pleo, Moss, and Spendesk, operating in 33 countries. The company retains 70% of its $100 million 2022 raise, which valued it at $1 billion. Additional investors include Greenoaks, Lightspeed, and QED. The funding supports global expansion.

item.title: Will Wright's MyMems Uses AI to Create Personal Memory-Based Games
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Will Wright's next simulation will use AI to mine content from your memories
Will Wright's new game MyMems will use generative AI to create personalized simulations from players' memories. Scheduled for release next year, the project marks a shift from Wright's past work with Maxis and EA. MyMems will extract memories to generate digital characters that form teams to solve puzzles, as described by Wright's Gallium Studios and partner Artificial Agency. Wright provided examples like imagining a scenario where his grandmother competes against Serena Williams. He criticized previous games like The Sims for failing to capture real-life nuances, such as understanding claustrophobia or family conflicts. MyMems will organize memories into themed zones like sports, vacations, and deaths, with options for shared memory-based worlds with others. The game aims to create deeply personal experiences by integrating players' lived experiences into its simulation.

item.title: WhatsApp Offers Alternative to Google Drive for Chat Backups
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Tired of WhatsApp backup eating away your Google Drive storage? They’ve got a solution now
WhatsApp is introducing a native cloud storage service for Android users, offering an alternative to Google Drive for chat backups. The update, discovered by WABetaInfo, allows users to store data directly on WhatsApp’s servers. Previously, Android users had to use Google Drive, which consumed Google account storage. The new option provides 2GB of free storage, with paid tiers like WhatsApp Plus (100GB) and Meta One (4TB) available. Backups are end-to-end encrypted by default, requiring users to set up encryption with a passkey or 64-digit key before initial backups. Paid subscribers retain the latest backup for up to four months after subscription lapses. The feature is currently available to Android beta testers via Google Play, with a broader rollout planned. This change gives users more control over data storage, separating chat records from Google Drive and freeing up space.

item.title: ULA Attributes Vulcan Rocket Failure to Fuel Supply Issues
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Vulcan failure caused by inadequate fuel supply to engines, ULA says
United Launch Alliance attributed the Vulcan rocket's Sunday launch failure to inadequate fuel supply to the BE-4 engines, not engine performance. ULA stated preliminary analysis of flight data indicated low booster thrust resulted from insufficient fuel delivery, confirming earlier reports from Ars Technica. The finding provides relief to Blue Origin and NASA, as the BE-4 engine is central to Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket. New Glenn faced a ground test failure in May linked to a main oxygen valve issue, which Blue Origin addressed with retrofits. The Vulcan investigation exonerated the BE-4 engine, allowing Blue Origin to proceed with its return-to-flight plan for New Glenn, potentially as early as January. Blue Origin acknowledged collaboration with ULA, stating the fuel supply issue was unrelated to engine performance and expressing confidence in Vulcan's recovery.

item.title: Retro Song Bird Lets Game Boy Cartridges Play Soundtracks Directly
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Retro Kickstarter speaker can play soundtracks directly from original Game Boy cartridges
The Retro Song Bird is a Kickstarter-funded device that plays Game Boy and Game Boy Color cartridge soundtracks directly. It functions as a box-shaped speaker with physical controls for navigation and volume, supporting over 1,900 games. The device offers register-level sound emulation, allowing users to isolate audio channels via USB audio streams for use in digital audio workstations. It also supports LSDj for chiptune playback and syncs two units for DJ-style performances. Additional features include Game Boy Camera webcam functionality, save file backup, and export of soundtracks as WAV files. The device includes an open API, over-the-air updates, and an alarm mode. Priced at $79 for the standard model, with a sold-out $59 Early Bird offer, the two-unit bundle costs $150. Shipments are scheduled for April 2027. The developer notes limited prototypes exist, and manufacturing challenges like component availability and injection-molded enclosure production remain. Backers are warned about potential delays and uncertain delivery timelines.

item.title: Best Buy sells Blu-rays online and in-store again
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica
Best Buy is resuming Blu-ray and DVD sales through its website and physical stores after previously discontinuing the practice in 2023. The website currently lists 15 Blu-rays, including new releases like The Odyssey (2026) and older titles such as The Godfather (1972). Most titles are available for online purchase with delivery or in-store pickup. The Odyssey is listed as available for pickup within an hour at some stores. Best Buy had stopped selling Blu-rays and DVDs online and in stores starting in 2024, citing the evolving media consumption habits. A spokesperson noted the change allows the company to focus on new technologies. Last year, Best Buy began selling Blu-rays and DVDs from third-party sellers via its marketplace. Other retailers like Target and Disney have also scaled back or ended their Blu-ray and DVD operations.

item.title: AI-driven security patches causing widespread tech outages
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: AI May Be Breaking Everything Because It’s Finding Too Many Things to Fix
AI-driven security patches are causing widespread tech outages as systems struggle to handle rapid vulnerability fixes. The NSA and Wall Street executives told Congress that recent disruptions were linked to efforts to address AI-discovered flaws. A congressional official noted that AI models are identifying massive vulnerabilities, forcing urgent patches that systems were not designed to handle. Microsoft’s Nov. 12 outage, FAA’s ground stop, and JPMorgan’s banking issues were attributed to software bugs or overwhelmed infrastructure. The NSA’s outage was tied to PHP vulnerabilities found by AI. Sen. Mark Warner said the incidents stem from AI’s impact on cybersecurity, not cyberattacks. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin warned of Iranian-linked attacks on critical infrastructure, though current outages appear technical. Cybersecurity expert Nicole Perlroth highlighted reliance on complex, poorly understood systems. The FAA and Microsoft have offered alternative explanations, but experts warn the problem could worsen as AI accelerates vulnerability discovery.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: 12 Tech Components Worth Salvaging for Projects and Repairs
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: 12 salvaged components from old tech worth keeping in your spare parts bin
Old tech components can be valuable for DIY projects and repairs. Laptop displays can be repurposed for portable monitors or smart mirrors but require matching controller boards and touch digitizers. Webcams can serve as security cameras or pet monitors, though voltage conversion may be needed. Power adapters with barrel jacks are useful for LED strips and devices, with polarity checks essential. LED backlights from TVs can provide bright lighting or DIY light panels but need specialized drivers. Hard drive magnets are strong and suitable for holders, though disassembly requires care. Storage drives like SSDs and HDDs can be reused for upgrades or NAS systems, especially with current memory shortages. Wi-Fi cards from motherboards can replace dead cards or add connectivity, though Intel CNVi cards have compatibility limits. Stepper motors from old printers or CD drives are prized for CNC machines and robots, though newer devices often use DC motors. PC fans offer cooling solutions for devices or air purifiers. Sensors like IR receivers and motion detectors can be salvaged for projects or repairs. Each component requires specific handling, wiring, or compatibility checks for reuse.

item.title: Google Home Update Lets Users Unlock Doors Digitally
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Google Home’s latest update could make your house keys a thing of the past
Google Home's latest update introduces digital key access via Google Wallet for Android users with compatible smart locks. Users can unlock doors by tapping phones against locks or using contactless methods. Security cameras now provide sound context for motion events, helping users assess situations without immediate video review. Gemini for Home responds 20% faster to routine commands and expands to six new markets. Nest thermostats in the U.S. and Canada will show energy savings estimates starting December. The fourth-gen Nest Learning Thermostat supports third-party temperature sensors for better room-specific climate control. Google emphasizes incremental improvements to existing smart home tools rather than overhauling the ecosystem, aiming to enhance daily convenience for users invested in its platform.

item.title: AI Identified Critical Java Vulnerability Using 'AAAAAAAA...' String
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: AI found a hole in Java, and it starts with 'AAAAAAAA...'
AI identified a critical Java vulnerability using a string of 'A' characters. Researchers at Calif, aided by OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber model, discovered the flaw allows hackers to trigger memory errors in Java's base64 decoder. Exploiting this could grant unauthorized system access, demonstrated on Keycloak, a login system used by CERN and NASA. Java powers 90% of Fortune 500 companies, including banks, hospitals, and government agencies. Oracle released a patch update, and CISA urged immediate fixes. However, unpatched systems may remain vulnerable for five to 10 years. While officials haven't linked recent outages to AI, the incident highlights aging digital infrastructure's risks. The 'AAAAAAAA...' string now symbolizes a potential entry point for attacks in an escalating cybersecurity landscape.

item.title: DDR6 RAM Shrinks 44% While Boosting Bandwidth to 4X DDR5's Baseline
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: DDR6 RAM shrinks by 44% while delivering 4X DDR5's baseline bandwidth — JEDEC previews 12.8 GT/s modules with up to 1 terabyte of capacity per slot
JEDEC previews DDR6 RAM modules, which will be 44% shorter than DDR5 at 74mm. DDR6 will operate at 12.8 GT/s, quadrupling DDR5's baseline bandwidth to 153.6 GB/s. The data bus width expands to 96 bits, a 50% increase over DDR5's 64 bits. DDR6 modules could reach 1TB capacity per slot, with die stacking via Through-Silicon Vias (TSVs) enabling 128Gb (16GB) dies. Server DDR6 RDIMMs will start at DDR6-12800, surpassing DDR5's DDR5-9200. Consumer DDR6 speeds remain uncertain, though DDR5 began at DDR5-4800. DDR6 may adopt new pinouts and form factors like RDIMM, UDIMM, and CAMM, though pin counts are undisclosed. JEDEC anticipates commercialization by 2029, though delays are possible.

item.title: Waymo Halts San Francisco Robotaxi Service Due to Flooding
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Waymo pauses service in San Francisco after robotaxis get stuck on flooded streets
Waymo paused its San Francisco robotaxi service after vehicles became stuck in flooded streets, according to District 5 Supervisor Bilal Mahmood and the Waymo app. Riders received messages stating service was paused due to weather and would resume when road conditions improved. Heavy rain and an expected record El Niño winter have worsened flooding in the city. Videos showed Waymo vehicles blocking intersections, forcing cars to detour. The pause follows prior incidents, including a December 2025 power outage causing similar issues and a May 2026 recall of nearly 4,000 vehicles after a robotaxi drove into flooded streets in San Antonio. Waymo issued a software update but later paused service in Atlanta for the same issue. The company also pulled robotaxis from California freeways after the DMV restricted access, effective immediately.

item.title: Ransomware Group Claims to Have Stolen Data from Nvidia Partner
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Nvidia Probes Breach of Partner As Ransomware Group Claims It Stole Data
Nvidia is investigating whether a third-party partner was breached after a ransomware group called The Gentlemen claimed to have stolen data. The group listed Nvidia as a recent victim and demanded payment to prevent data leaks, though no stolen data has been released. Nvidia told PCMag it is examining an incident affecting a partner but found no evidence its own systems were compromised. The Gentlemen also claimed to breach Taiwan-based Jentech Precision Industrial, an Nvidia partner for AI cooling. Jentech did not comment. The Gentlemen, active since mid-2025, rents out ransomware attacks and uses double extortion tactics, encrypting data while exfiltrating sensitive information to pressure victims, according to Microsoft.

item.title: China Reveals GJ-11 Stealth Drone with Internal Weapons and Stealth Design
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: China goes public with stealth UAV manned by crack team of 'self-trained female drone operators' — GJ-11 looks a lot like Northrop Grumman's X-47B now-defunct UCAV
China released television footage of its GJ-11 stealth combat drone, showcasing internal weapons compartments, retractable landing gear, and nose-mounted sensors. The aircraft is designed for airstrikes and suppression of enemy air defenses, featuring two internal weapon bays capable of carrying 1,000 to 2,000 pounds of munitions. Its stealth configuration includes a flattened exhaust outlet and tailless flying-wing design to reduce radar and infrared signatures. The GJ-11's structure mirrors Northrop Grumman's X-47B in shape and internal weapons layout, though the American drone never entered service. Footage showed the drone operating alongside J-16 and J-20 fighters, suggesting integrated combat roles. Development traces back to the Sharp Sword demonstrator, with public debut during a 2019 parade and subsequent testing in Xinjiang and Tibet. The aircraft's autonomous capabilities and data-sharing between platforms remain undisclosed.

item.title: Java vulnerability enables remote code execution in millions of systems
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Critical Java vulnerability puts millions of sites, services, and devices at risk of remote code execution
A critical Java vulnerability, dubbed Java4Shell, allows remote code execution without authentication, enabling attackers to access systems, steal data, and take control. The flaw, found in OpenJDK's Base64 decoding optimization, was rated 9.2 on the CVSS 4.0 scale and ranges from 8 to 9.8 across vendors. Exploits require Java running on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 and VBMI support, affecting Intel Ice Lake and AMD Zen 4 chips. Attackers can trigger the bug by inputting 64 'A's and an '=' sign, overwriting memory like the Heartbleed vulnerability. Oracle has patched the issue, but widespread Java usage means many systems remain vulnerable, including Keycloak, Jira, Elasticsearch, and container images. The vulnerability was discovered by an AI bot using $200 in tokens, highlighting its depth despite not being a low-hanging fruit. Affected systems include enterprise software, databases, and cloud services, with remediation efforts ongoing across vendors like IBM, Red Hat, and Broadcom.

item.title: Sacrebleu launches $1,700 smart lighting console with physical controls
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Sacrebleu launches a $1,700 smart lighting console with a physical knob and motorized sliders
Sacrebleu launches the F4, a $1,700 smart lighting console with physical knobs and motorized sliders. The device, inspired by 1970s hi-fi equipment, allows users to control smart lights via tactile controls. Founder Alex Dufetel initially built the console for his home, later sharing it online where it gained two million views. The F4 features four motorized faders that adjust automatically when brightness is changed via phone or wall switch. It supports Philips Hue, Lutron Caséta, Sonos, and other systems through Home Assistant. The console also includes four preset keys, a touchscreen, and a solid walnut body. Pre-orders are open with the first 20 units sold at $1,600, and 100 units expected to ship in Q2 2027. Availability is limited to the U.S. and Canada for now, with an international waitlist.

item.title: Tony Gilroy Wants Lucasfilm to Continue Andor Story
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Tony Gilroy Hopes Lucasfilm Picks Up the Story of ‘Andor’
Tony Gilroy hopes Lucasfilm will continue the story of 'Andor,' the Star Wars series he created. He emphasized the show's rich canon and characters, including a child born to Cassian Andor and Bix Caleen, which could explore rebellious or imperial paths. The child's age aligns with key Star Wars eras, allowing narratives spanning the Age of Rebellion, New Republic, and Rise of the First Order. Gilroy, who finished a new movie with Pedro Pascal, has no interest in returning to Star Wars but is open to others continuing his characters. Lucasfilm president Dave Filoni could decide the child's fate, though no official plans exist. Gilroy stressed he’s no longer involved with Lucasfilm and has no control over future developments.

item.title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Neon AI Model, Outperforms Rivals in Key Metrics
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon AI model, rivals Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol
Google has launched Gemini 4 Neon, a new AI model positioned between Gemini 4 Carbon and Hydrogen. Available to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers via the Gemini app, API, and Android Studio, Neon offers deeper analysis capabilities. Priced at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, it features a 1 million token context window and four thinking levels, with 'high' as default. Neon outperforms Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol on the Vals Index (70.9%) and AutomationBench (56.3%), but lags behind on Terminal-Bench 4.1 and FrontierCode 2.0. Logan Kilpatrick noted Neon's 'right mix of intelligence, speed and usability.' Google claims Neon matches Carbon's performance at 32% lower cost per task. The model handles complex tasks like spreadsheet analysis, PDF processing, and integrates with Gmail and Docs via Gemini Tasks. Pro and Ultra users gain access to Orchestrator mode, combining Neon's planning with Hydrogen's execution.

item.title: Researchers show anonymous messaging accounts can be linked to personal profiles
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Anonymous messaging apps may not be as private as you think
Researchers from the University of Maryland and KAIST demonstrated how anonymous messaging accounts can be linked to personal profiles using existing app features. Their study, presented at the 2026 Network and Distributed System Security Symposium, tested KakaoTalk, Telegram, WhatsApp, Signal, and Tinder. The team used contact discovery and nearby user search tools, along with phone numbers and profile pictures, to connect anonymous accounts to real identities. A phone number serves as the primary link, allowing attackers to cross-reference legal names across platforms. Profile pictures further narrow down locations, with tests showing an average radius of 324 meters. Yonghwi Kwon, a co-author, noted these features are often overlooked as harmless but can collectively expose user data. KakaoTalk, which serves 94% of South Korea’s population, is particularly vulnerable, while the U.S. market’s app diversity offers more protection. KakaoTalk has since restricted the methods described. Users are advised to use distinct photos for anonymous accounts, delete old profiles, and use separate phone numbers for sensitive services.

item.title: Ukraine Destroys Kerch Bridge Using Relay Drones
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Ukraine blew up Putin’s bridge using relay drones to bypass Starlink limits
Ukraine's military struck the Kerch Strait Bridge on November 15-16, damaging a steel arch and blocking automobile traffic. The attack used relay drones equipped with mesh radios to create an airborne communications network, allowing operators over 250 kilometers away to guide missiles and drones without relying on Starlink. Ukrainian forces employed homegrown Flamingo cruise missiles and overwhelmed Russian air defenses. The operation followed weeks of preparatory strikes targeting Russian air defense systems and radars. The attack coincided with the largest Ukrainian overnight drone strike on Russia since the war began. Russian sources claimed hundreds of drones preceded the strike, enabling remote-controlled missile attacks. The Financial Times noted Ukraine adapted a Russian battlefield tactic by using the mesh network to bypass electronic warfare and guide weapons to the bridge's structural weaknesses.

item.title: Google Chrome Adds AI Scam Detection via Screenshots
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Google Chrome’s new screenshot-based AI scam detection feature is hitting me with déjà vu
Google is expanding Chrome's security features with a new AI-driven scam detection tool that uses browser-side screenshots to identify deceptive websites. The feature, part of Enhanced Safe Browsing, employs visual classification to analyze page layouts and detect threats, including recently registered scam domains not yet in blocklists. Unlike Windows Recall, which stores screenshots locally, Chrome's system will transmit images to its servers for analysis, raising privacy concerns. The capability is limited to users who opt into Enhanced Safe Browsing, excluding standard Safe Browsing participants. By combining visual data with browsing context, the tool aims to catch scams that evade traditional URL or code-based detection methods. Google's approach seeks to address the challenge of rapidly evolving phishing sites that mimic legitimate layouts.
